subject: US region degraded — temporary fallback instructions and next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acme-retail.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-09-17T07:12:00Z
Subject: US region degraded — temporary fallback instructions and next steps

Hi team,

We are seeing elevated 5xx errors and increased tail latency originating in the US-east (us-east-1) zone starting ~07:05 UTC. Our serving telemetry shows request drops in the regional egress path to the cloud provider; model execution and KV cache remain healthy for requests that get through.

Immediate action for affected customers (short checklist):
- If you can, shift write/produce traffic to a different region (us-west-2 or eu-west-1) via the region override: add the SDK parameter region="us-west-2" or set header X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2.
- If you cannot change region, enable soft-fallback by adding query param ?region_fallback=true to your API calls. This will route to the closest compatible model variant in a different region.
- Temporarily increase client-side retry backoff to 300–800ms (exponential backoff) and avoid aggressive parallel retries.

Example cURL for a quick switch:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2' -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","prompt":"..."}'

We attached a small runbook with exact SDK flags and sample configs (runbook-incident-20290917.pdf).

We will provide a follow-up with ETA once the cloud provider provides a mitigation timeline. For now, please apply the region override if feasible — that will restore normal latency for most requests.

Apologies for the disruption. I will update this thread as we learn more.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: ops@acme-retail.com
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-09-17T07:28:00Z
Subject: Re: US region degraded — temporary fallback instructions and next steps

Thanks Rafael — we see the spike on our side as well. Two quick clarifying questions:
1) Do you have an ETA for when the us-east path will be stable?
2) Are embeddings and batch ingest affected the same way as interactive generation?

We can flip region on a small subset but would like to understand impact before moving prod.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acme-retail.com, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-09-17T08:05:00Z
Subject: Re: US region degraded — temporary fallback instructions and next steps

Priya — short answers:
- ETA: We are tracking the cloud provider mitigation ticket. Their latest update is 2–4 hours for staged mitigation; we will share updates as they confirm.
- Embeddings: embeddings ingest is hitting the same egress path for some hosts. Small-batch embeddings are OK if routed to us-west-2; large parallel ingest jobs may experience throttling in us-east.

Suggested immediate plan from ops side (minimal change):
1) Add X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2 header for a small canary (5–10% traffic) to validate fallbacks.
2) For batch jobs, schedule a short pause and resubmit to region=us-west-2 when convenient.
3) If you see client-side 5xxs, enable region_fallback=true to allow automatic reroute.

We have added a monitoring check and will open a dedicated status link once the provider posts their mitigations (link will be in a later update).

Marissa
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-09-18T13:30:00Z
Subject: Incident update: provider mitigation applied / traffic normalization

Team — closing the active mitigation window summary:
- Cloud provider reports they applied a network control-plane change at ~2029-09-18T11:50Z that corrected the egress path anomalies.
- Telemetry shows error-rate returning to baseline over the next 90 minutes; ~95% of affected clients normalized after automatic fallback.
- We ingested incident-level logs into the incident archive (incident-logs-20290917.json).

Action items before customer postmortem:
- Draft customer-facing summary and proposed credits (if SLA triggers). Owner: Lauren (ETA 48 hours).
- Internal root-cause analysis (network path + provider confirmation). Owner: Marcus (ETA 72 hours).
- Verify all canary toggles default back to normal region-selection in 24 hours. Owner: Marissa (ETA 24 hours).

I attached a trimmed log export for review. Let me know if we missed any affected dataset or partner route.

— Soojin
Incident Response Lead

From: ops@acme-retail.com

Date: 2029-09-19T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: US region degraded — temporary fallback instructions and next steps

Thanks for the updates — most of our traffic normalized after switching to us-west-2. We did see a handful of failed batch jobs that require manual re-run.

Two asks:
1) Can we schedule a short post-incident call to confirm scope and credits?
2) Please share the timeline of the provider mitigation and any logs you used to determine client impact.

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acme-retail.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-09-19T16:45:00Z
Subject: Post-incident summary & customer next steps (ACME) — Sept 17 outage

Priya / Acme team — thank you for your patience. Below is the customer-facing post-incident summary and concrete next steps. We will publish a public short-form notice once Acme OKs the text.

Summary (brief):
- Impact window: 2029-09-17T07:05Z -> 2029-09-18T13:30Z (errors spiked in us-east-1; provider mitigation applied 2029-09-18T11:50Z).
- User impact: elevated request errors and higher latency for customers primarily routed to us-east-1. Customers that applied region override or region_fallback saw service continuity.
- Root cause (high level): transient provider egress path failure affecting our regional routing — working with provider for RCA.

Customer next steps and offers:
- We recommend teams keep the region override steps in their runbooks for fast mitigation. The runbook is attached.
- We will offer a goodwill credit equal to one day of service for customers who saw >=10% error rate during the window. Please confirm if you want Redwood to apply that credit to your billing account.
- Schedule: We propose a 30-minute call to review scope, timeline, and credits. Suggested times: 2029-09-20 15:00 UTC or 2029-09-21 09:00 UTC. Tell us which works for you.

Internal action items (owners):
- Customer note and credit proposal to Acme (Lauren) — post the short summary to Customer Success and apply credits after confirmation.
- Full technical RCA with packet-level timelines (Marcus) — deliverable: incident RCA doc (Drive link below).
- Update public status page and add a short blurb to the incident archive (Marissa).

Attachments: postmortem-sept17-2029.pdf, customer-credits-template.docx
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeF-incident-20290917, HubSpot:HS-23145

Please reply to confirm the call time and if you would like the credit applied. Once agreed, we will schedule the internal RCA review with your engineering team.

Thanks again — we take outages seriously and will follow up with the full technical postmortem.

— Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
